sentences.text: Ilbandornis was an extinct genus of birds about the size of an ostrich, possessing a lighter build than other dromornithids that suggests it was a fast runner.
The dromornithid family is casually called "demon ducks" because they are closely related to waterfowl.
Patricia Vickers-Rich named two species of Ilbandornis in 1979, establishing the genus after finding fossils in the Waite Formation at the Alcoota Fossil Beds in Australia's Northern Territory.
Most researchers believe Ilbandornis was herbivorous, supported by molecular analysis of its gastroliths and eggshells.

Ilbandornis belongs to the family Dromornithidae, though some researchers debate whether Ilbandornis lawsoni should remain in its own genus or be classified as a species of Genyornis or synonymous with I. woodburnei.

Fossils of Ilbandornis date to the Late Miocene, yet the fossil record spans from the Tortonian to the Late Pleistocene, between 11.63 and 0.0117 million years ago, indicating the animal went extinct during the Miocene epoch according to one view.
